meta.disclaimer: Indicative estimate based on self-reported inputs and published industry benchmarks. Figures illustrate the scale of opportunity and are not a guarantee of savings. A validated baseline requires assessment of actual billing data. Indicative and directional only. Not a commitment, quote or financial advice.

sources.label: Flexera 2026 State of the Cloud Report (n=753, March 2026)
sources.note: Wasted IaaS/PaaS spend 29% — the first increase in five years, attributed to AI workloads and new PaaS/SaaS pricing complexity. 63% of organisations run an established FinOps team; 71% operate a CCoE; 49% use unit economics. Fewer than half use any one commitment discount per provider.

sources.label: Flexera State of the Cloud, multi-year (2019–2026)
sources.note: Estimated waste has stayed within a 27–32% band every year since 2019 — the most stable benchmark available.

sources.label: Harness Cloud Cost Management Report (2025)
sources.note: 21% of infrastructure budget wasted on unused or underused resources; a useful conservative floor.

sources.label: FinOps Foundation, State of FinOps 2026
sources.note: Workload optimisation and waste reduction remain the top practitioner priority, but with diminishing returns — the large obvious waste has been captured.

benchmarks.honesty_note: Published waste benchmarks are reported cross-industry, not per-sector. Headline anchors below are global figures from named public sources. BFSI modifiers are LTM directional adjustments based on sector characteristics — not published sector waste rates — and are editable.

service_areas.name: FinOps Operating Model & Governance
service_areas.problem: No one is genuinely accountable for cloud spend, so decisions default to whoever notices the bill.
deliverables: FinOps charter and mandate, signed at executive level
Operating model design — centralised, federated or hybrid, with rationale
RACI across Engineering, Finance, Procurement and BU owners
Governance forum design, cadence and decision rights
Tooling assessment and platform recommendation
90-day mobilisation plan with named owners

service_areas.name: Cost Visibility & Allocation
service_areas.problem: Spend cannot be attributed to a team, product or customer, so no one can be held to it.
deliverables: Tagging and metadata taxonomy with enforcement policy
Cost allocation model including shared-cost treatment
Showback design, progressing to chargeback where appropriate
Executive and team-level cost dashboards
Automated cost data pipeline into enterprise BI
Allocation coverage baseline and improvement roadmap

service_areas.name: Forecasting, Budgets & Anomaly Control
service_areas.problem: The bill cannot be predicted, so Finance treats cloud as uncontrolled spend.
deliverables: Driver-based forecasting model with documented assumptions
Budget framework at BU and product level with forecast-breach alerting
Anomaly detection configuration and escalation routing
Monthly variance reporting pack and commentary standard
Forecast accuracy baseline and improvement target

service_areas.name: Commitment & Rate Optimisation
service_areas.problem: Paying on-demand rates for predictable, steady-state workloads.
deliverables: Commitment coverage analysis across providers
Commitment strategy and purchase calendar
Savings plan and reserved capacity portfolio design
Provider agreement and discount review
Ongoing coverage monitoring and renewal governance

service_areas.name: Workload & Architecture Optimisation
service_areas.problem: Resources are oversized, idle or orphaned, and nothing systematically reclaims them.
deliverables: Rightsizing assessment with prioritised savings backlog
Waste and orphaned-resource elimination programme
Storage tiering and lifecycle policy design
Non-production scheduling and automated parking
Spot and transient capacity adoption strategy
Architecture cost review standard for design gates

service_areas.name: Unit Economics & Value Realisation
service_areas.problem: Cloud spend cannot be defended to the board because its business value is not measured.
deliverables: Unit metric definition per product or service line
Cost-per-unit instrumentation and trending
Cloud business case validation against original assumptions
Margin and cost-to-serve analysis by customer or tenant
Board-level cloud value reporting pack

service_areas.name: FinOps Enablement & Capability Build
service_areas.problem: Cost awareness does not survive contact with delivery pressure unless it is built into how engineers work.
deliverables: FinOps role definitions and target capability model
Training curriculum and FinOps certification pathway
Cost-aware architecture and design standards
Engineering enablement — cost feedback in CI/CD and pull requests
Community of practice launch and operating rhythm

questions.text: Which best describes your infrastructure today?
questions.hint: Pick the closest match — precision is not required.

questions.text: Which cloud platforms are in use or planned?
questions.hint: Multi-cloud materially increases the cost of poor visibility.

questions.text: Roughly what is your annual cloud spend?
questions.hint: An order-of-magnitude estimate is enough. This drives the value calculation.

questions.text: Where are you in your cloud journey?
How do you expect cloud spend to change over the next 12 months?
What proportion of your remaining estate is still to move to cloud in the next 24 months?
questions.hint: Migrating on top of weak cost controls multiplies the problem rather than adding to it.

questions.text: Can you attribute cloud cost to a specific business unit, product or team?

options.label: Only at a very high level
No — it is one undifferentiated bill

questions.text: What percentage of your cloud resources carry complete, reliable tags or labels?
How long does it take to answer the question "why did the bill go up last month?"
questions.hint: This is the single most revealing question in the assessment.

options.label: Same day — the data is at hand
Weeks, and the answer is contested

questions.text: Do you know what it costs to serve one customer, transaction or unit of output?
Which of these do you receive on a regular, scheduled basis?
questions.hint: Select all that genuinely arrive without being chased.

options.label: Monthly cost report by team or product

questions.text: Over the last 12 months, how far did actual cloud spend differ from what was budgeted?
How often has an unexpected cloud bill required explanation to Finance or the board?
How confident are you in your cloud spend forecast for next quarter?
Who explains the cloud bill to Finance or the CFO?

options.label: A dedicated cost owner with the data to back it
No one — Finance interprets it themselves

questions.text: Who is formally accountable for cloud spend?

options.label: A named FinOps owner or team with a mandate
Each business unit owns its own consumption
The CIO or CTO, by default rather than design

questions.text: Distribute 100 points across where responsibility for cloud cost actually sits today.
questions.hint: Not where it should sit — where it genuinely does.

questions.text: To what extent do engineers see the cost consequences of what they build?
Is cost efficiency written into anyone's objectives or performance measures?
Which cost controls are actually operating today?
questions.hint: Select only those in live use, not those planned or configured but ignored.

questions.text: What proportion of eligible spend is covered by commitments — reserved instances, savings plans or committed use discounts?
When did you last systematically decommission unused or idle resources?

options.label: Never, or not that we know of

questions.text: Rank these cost concerns by how much they worry you — most concerning first.
questions.hint: This shapes where we focus, and is not scored against a right answer.
options: Inability to attribute cost to teams
Justifying cloud value to the board

questions.text: How actively do you monitor and optimize network data transfer (cross-AZ, cross-region, egress to on-premises/internet)?
questions.sub: Data transfer and network egress typically account for 10–25% of cloud infrastructure spend and often go unallocated.

options.label: Active architectural governance — private endpoints/interconnects, direct routes, and egress budget alerting
Standard monitoring in place, but egress spikes are investigated reactively
High-level awareness; egress is rarely tracked or attributed to specific workloads
Unmonitored — network data transfer is treated as an unmanaged baseline utility

questions.text: Can you demonstrate to the board that cloud spend is delivering business value?

options.label: The question has not been asked yet

questions.text: Has cloud delivered the savings or benefits set out in the original business case?

options.label: We do not track against the business case
There was no formal business case

questions.text: If Finance asked today whether cloud spend was under control, how comfortable would you be answering?
What would a good outcome look like in 12 months?
questions.hint: Used to shape the recommendations, not scored.

A position we can defend to Finance
